verdict: The panel is clean and consistent (lime main action, red end run, x in the corner), but the screen's real job, 'press a' after a pad was lost, is a small title above a pause menu, so the player can't tell what happened or what to do.

findings.what: The prompt that is the whole point of this screen is a ~32px title in the same style as any menu title. It is not the hero, it is not near the lime action, and nothing says a pad was lost or whose pad it is. A player sees a pause menu with an odd heading. 'press a' also sits above 'resume', which reads as two competing instructions.
findings.fix: Make the live prompt the hero: 56px f-cond 800 tx-1, centred above the buttons, with a 16px tx-2 label above it that names the player and the cause (e.g. 'p2 pad lost'). Drop 'press a' from the title slot and use 'paused' or the player label there. Put a pad glyph for the button on the resume button.

findings.what: The card is a 480x485 island in a 1920x1080 black void, about 11% of the screen area. This breaks the settled rule of a centred card taking nearly the whole screen (Q43, 90% width). From a couch it is small, and the 20px button text is lost in the black space. The background is pure black with no raid visible, so the scrim (.80) is not read as a pause over a live game.
findings.fix: If this stays a compact pause card, scale it up to about 640x720 with 24px button text and 72px rows, or follow the guide and go to a 90% card. Show the frozen raid behind a .80 scrim rather than flat #0b0c0d.

findings.where: button stack (resume, settings, report a problem, feedback, what's new)
findings.what: Five actions plus end run, in three different row layouts (one full-width lime, two full-width ghost, a 50/50 pair, then a bare text link). Three of them (report a problem, feedback, what's new) are not pause actions and are clutter on a screen that is supposed to say 'press a'. Report a problem and feedback do nearly the same job, which breaks the one control per job rule.
findings.fix: Keep resume, settings, end run. Move report a problem, feedback and what's new into settings or a single 'more' row. If they stay, make them one consistent full-width ghost row each at 56px high with 16px gaps.

findings.what: The destructive action is a bare 20px red text link with no border or hit area, 30px below the last button, floating on its own. It has no pad focus affordance. Red text on #16191b is only about 4:1 and thin. Nothing marks it as something to confirm.
findings.fix: Give it the ghost button shape with a 1px --danger border and --danger text at 20px 600. Align it to the same 400px column and 56px height, 24px below the stack, and label the confirm step on press.

findings.what: Only resume is shown as focused (lime fill). The idle buttons have a border barely brighter than the card, around 1.5:1 against it, so rows read as faint outlines. There is no visible difference between a hover or focus on a ghost button and idle, so pad navigation can't be judged from this frame.
findings.fix: Idle border --ui-line-hi #4a5257 at 1px with a --ui-raised fill. Focus: 2px --acc border plus a 3px lime left bar. Keep the lime fill only for the one primary action, not for the focused row.

findings.what: The 36px accent tab at the top-left edge sits at about 40% opacity and reads as a rendering glitch. It is dull olive, not lime, and it is flush with the border at the card's corner with nothing aligned to it.
findings.fix: Draw it at full --acc, 3px high and 36px wide, inset exactly flush on the border, or delete it. The guide allows the tab only on a 'star' panel.

findings.what: The x icon is a thin 26px stroke in muted grey with no hit box or hover. The title baseline (y 350) and the x centre (y 346) are off by about 4px. The divider sits only 30px under the title and 24px above the first button, so the header spacing is uneven against the 16px gaps below.
findings.fix: Draw the x in a 40x40 box, centred on the title's cap height, in --tx-2 with a --ui-raised hover fill. Use a 56px header row with the divider at its bottom edge and 24px to the first button.

findings.what: The padding under 'end run' is about 48px against 40px at the top and 40px at the sides, so the bottom looks heavy. The card is also drawn on a 1px border with a faint gradient, which the guide bans.
findings.fix: Set the padding to 24px on all four sides of the card, with end run 24px from the bottom edge. Use a flat --ui-panel fill with no gradient.
